newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index slips after cracking 6,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index slips after cracking 6,000 level.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average pushed through 6,000 points Monday for the first time but then succumbed to mild profit-taking.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow was off 7.08 points at 5,985.78 after peaking at 6,002.17.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on volume of 218 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 1.46 at 1,249.02 and the American Stock Exchange index gained 2.08 at 581.97. The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 1.16 to 702.62.
Analysts said blue-chip stocks were vulnerable to profit-taking, particularly after Friday's rally lifted the Dow by 60 points to a new closing high of 5,992.86.
"We had a dramatic move on Friday," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "This is nothing more than a little profit-taking."
Analysts said stocks appeared to have more room to rise before their next major pause.
"The momentum is in place, so any pullback will probably be viewed as short-term, shallow and a buying opportunity," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
According to one measure, the Dow's achievement apparently occurred in the same week that the stock market's bull run began, six years ago.

In a research note, Lehman Brothers chief investment strategist Jeffrey Applegate pointed to Oct. 11, 1990, when the S&P 500 closed at 295.46, its lowest close in that cycle, as the starting point for a bull run that has seen the index more than double to just over 700.

The Dow's climb on Monday was helped by a strong showing in component Texaco Inc. after the oil company confirmed it was discussing linking its U.S. refining and marketing operations with those of Shell Oil Co. Texaco was up 1-5/8 to 97-1/4.

Treasury bonds backtracked after Friday's powerful rally, with the 30-year bond off 9/32 to yield 6.77 percent. The 30-year bond soared more than a full point Friday, knocking its yield down to 6.75 percent from 6.84 percent at Thursday's close.
The interest-rate sensitive financial and transportation sectors were both weaker, with J.P. Morgan & Co. off 1/2 to 87-1/2, Citicorp down 5/8 to 91-7/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp. off 5/8 to 81-1/8.
American Airlines parent, AMR Corp. fell 1 to 82-1/2 and railroad company Burlington Northern Santa Fe Corp. fell 7/8 to 84-1/2.
Augat Inc. jumped 4-3/8 to 25-1/4 after agreeing to be acquired by Thomas & Betts. Thomas & Betts, which valued the all-stock deal at $550 million, fell 1-3/4 to 38.
